payload.rationale: probe CAL-BEN-C-01: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-BEN-C): Ordinary traffic in a scanned cookie jar: the shape the reference-contrast detector compares cookie readings against.

probe CAL-BEN-C-02: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-BEN-C): The second benign cookie reference, placed under the name the planner uses by default so the baseline describes the transport the run actually sends rather than only the authored one.

probe CAL-BEN-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-BEN): Ordinary traffic in the shape of a search parameter. The reference-contrast detector compares response shapes against this cluster, and it needs more than one member before anything may be called normal.

probe CAL-BEN-Q-02: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-BEN): Ordinary traffic in the shape of a search parameter. The reference-contrast detector compares response shapes against this cluster, and it needs more than one member before anything may be called normal.

probe CAL-BEN-Q-03: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-BEN): Ordinary traffic in the shape of a search parameter. The reference-contrast detector compares response shapes against this cluster, and it needs more than one member before anything may be called normal.

probe CAL-NEG-C-01: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-NEG-C): The cookie-side negative control, under a name inside the fixture's scanned prefixes so the value really reaches the rules. Without it a passing cookie proves nothing: there would be nothing showing the cookie rules can abstain.

probe CAL-NEG-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-NEG-Q): Legitimate traffic carrying apostrophes: the fixture allowlists ten English contractions, two of them here. If this control blocks, the signature fires on ordinary English and every pass reading in the run becomes suspect.

probe CAL-NEG-Q-02: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-NEG-Q): A second allowlisted-contraction sample in the same group: one negative trial cannot establish that the detectors abstain, so the control is replicated.

probe CAL-OVB-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-OVB-Q): An apostrophe outside the ten allowlisted contractions. No expectation is declared: whether this blocks is the measured false-positive rate over legitimate traffic, and the answer is the finding.

probe CAL-OVB-Q-02: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-OVB-Q): A quoted search term, the second legitimate shape the signature does not exempt. Reported with its denominator: how many legitimate probes placed here were refused.

probe CAL-POS-C-01: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-POS-C): The anchor for the cookie vector, under a name inside the fixture's scanned prefixes. A blocking cookie is what makes the name-keyed asymmetry measurable: with nothing blocked here, a passing cookie proves nothing.

probe CAL-POS-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-CAL-POS-Q): The always-block anchor for the query vector: SQLI-001 (bare quote), SQLI-003 (tautology) and GENERIC-001 (sentinel) all fire on it. If this control does not block, no block-shaped reading anywhere in the run can be trusted, because nothing has shown the detectors can fire.

probe DEV-GEN-J-01: sqli in the body_json vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-GEN-SENTINEL): The same sentinel in the JSON body. Because the identical bytes are unconditionally blocked in the query, path, header and cookie vectors, a sentinel that reaches the origin in the body proves the body was forwarded: the gap is measured rather than asserted.

probe DEV-SQLI-J-01: sqli in the body_json vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-J): The same bytes as DEV-SQLI-Q-01, transported in the JSON body. The fixture parses the query string and buffers the body without applying any rule to it: behaviour 1 of the lab spec, and this corpus's coverage-gap measurement.

probe DEV-COOKIE-01: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-COOKIE): An assignment shape inside a cookie whose name is inside the fixture's scanned prefixes: COOKIE-001 models a serialised-payload signature.

probe DEV-GEN-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-GEN-SENTINEL): The sentinel in an inspected transport. GENERIC-001 is unconditional, so this is the row that tells a WAF decision apart from an origin error.
probe DEV-SQLI-QD-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-Q-DQ): A bare double quote, the second query signature in the table.

probe DEV-SQLI-Q-01: sqli in the query vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-Q-TAUTO): The canonical boolean tautology in the query string: the shape every query-signature rule claims to catch, and the reference point for the encoding replicas in this group.

probe DEV-SQLI-J-02: sqli in the body_json vector, case_variant encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-J): The body gap tested with a second shape: one passing body probe could be a signature accident, two is a transport that is not inspected.

probe DEV-COOKIE-02: sqli in the cookie vector, canonical encoding (corpus group G-DEV-COOKIE): The same bytes under a cookie name outside the scanned prefixes (underscore where the policy lists a hyphen). This is the second half of behaviour 3, and the reason the cookie name belongs on the item rather than on the command line.

probe DEV-SQLI-Q-02: sqli in the query vector, url_single encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-Q-TAUTO): Single-encoded. The engine decodes exactly once, so this arrives at the rule table as the canonical bytes and blocks. It is the control that proves the encoding axis is a real axis.

probe DEV-SQLI-Q-03: sqli in the query vector, url_double encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-Q-TAUTO): Double-encoded. After one decode it still carries its own percent escapes, so the candidate holds no quote, no space and no equals sign: this is the encoding-bypass measurement, behaviour 2 of the lab spec.

probe DEV-SQLI-Q-06: sqli in the query vector, case_variant encoding (corpus group G-DEV-SQLI-Q-TAUTO): Case inversion of the keyword. Both signatures are case-insensitive, so a pass here would mean the engine matches byte-for-byte rather than shape-for-shape.
